body.statement: For one normalized conjunction, the single-conjunction representative transition is sound and complete: within any block, all values outside the distinct intervention constants induce the same refinement and future support, so one fresh value suffices. Across all branching blocks the number of representative column choices is at most \(3^{h/3}\). For \(r\) normalized conjunctions, the joint-score representative transition is sound and complete after truth flags are included, and the number of representative column choices is at most \((r+1)^h\).
body.justification: The representative bounds convert normalized-state sufficiency into alphabet-independent transition complexity.
body.gap: Published response-signature and finite-model algorithms enumerate alphabet-indexed function values rather than quotienting untested constants within each normalized prefix block.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a complete branching rule that scans large alphabets only polynomially.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=i+1\), and first consider a block \(T\in\pi_i\) for one normalized conjunction. By \texttt{thm:partition-continuation}, all natural worlds in \(T\) call one response row. If there is no natural world, the column on \(T\) is fixed by interventions. If factual or conjunction pins on natural worlds in \(T\) require two distinct values, the transition is infeasible; if they require one value, the natural output is fixed and the block does not branch.

In the remaining case let \(C_T\) be the set of distinct intervention constants in \(T\). For any \(z,z'\in\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), the natural worlds form one successor subblock distinct from every intervention-constant subblock under either choice. Thus \(z\) and \(z'\) induce the same partition refinement and violate no current natural pin. The continuation theorem gives the same future support. A choice in \(C_T\), by contrast, merges the natural subblock with the worlds bearing that constant and is retained separately. Hence retaining every element of \(C_T\) and one scanned element of \(\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), when the latter set is nonempty, is sound and complete, including singleton and exhausted alphabets.

If a branching block contains \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds and has size \(t=a+b\), its representative count is at most \(a+1\leq t\). For integer \(t=1,2,3\), direct calculation gives \(t\leq3^{t/3}\). For \(t\geq3\), the function \(x\mapsto\log(x)/x\) is decreasing, so
\[
 \frac{\log t}{t}\leq\frac{\log3}{3},
 \qquad
 t\leq3^{t/3}.
\]
If \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\) are the sizes of the branching blocks, then they are disjoint subsets of \(\mathcal H\), and therefore
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^m t_j
 \leq3^{\sum_jt_j/3}
 \leq3^{h/3}.
 \tag{3}
\]
No subtraction of one from \(h\) is valid when the normalized context set omits the factual context and its factual-equivalent block is empty.

For the joint compiler, attach a flag vector \(a_i\in\{0,1\}^r\) to the partition. At a fixed world-coordinate, coalesce repeated identical tests within each live term. If one live term tests two distinct constants there, its flag must become zero at this coordinate, so set it to zero before constructing representatives. This value-preserving preprocessing leaves at most one tested constant for each live-term/world pair.

For an unpinned natural group in \(T\), let \(C_T\) now contain all distinct intervention constants and all constants tested there by still-live terms. Two outputs outside \(C_T\) have the same equality relation to every intervention constant and fail exactly the same current tests. They therefore induce the same successor partition and flag vector, and \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} gives identical future support. Retaining the elements of \(C_T\cap\mathcal D_q\) and one fresh alphabet value, when available, is consequently sound and complete. Every retained representative is legal exactly when its direct intervention, factual, and test checks pass, and the row construction in the continuation theorem realizes it.

If \(T\) has \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds, then there are at most \(a+rb+1\) representatives. With \(t=a+b\) and \(r\geq1\),
\[
 a+rb+1\leq rt+1\leq(r+1)^t,
\]
where the last inequality retains the constant and linear terms in the binomial expansion. Multiplying over disjoint branching blocks gives
\[
 \prod_T(r+1)^{|T|}\leq(r+1)^h.
 \tag{4}
\]
The flag update is conjunction with exactly the current coordinate's tests. Hence a zero flag needs no further information, while a live flag records exactly that all processed tests have passed. Equality of the partition and flags is therefore a right congruence for future transitions. Equations (3)--(4) prove the corrected representative counts and the preceding arguments prove soundness and completeness.
